description: Verify that DUT-emitted ARP Probes target a Link-Local address in the usable 169.254.[1-254].* range — first/last 256 addresses are reserved (RFC 3927 §2.1, MUST)
approach:
[Objective]
RFC 3927 §2.1 reserves the first 256 (169.254.0.0/24) and the last 256 (169.254.255.0/24) addresses of the Link-Local prefix. Implementations MUST pick from the usable 169.254.1.0..169.254.254.255 range. This case observes the first DUT-emitted ARP Probe and asserts the target IP falls inside the usable range.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: OpStartLLAutoconf (kicks the Link-Local state machine)

2. Observation:
   • DUT → wire: ARP Probe (the first one)
     - target_proto_ip ∈ 169.254.[1..254].*   ← key check

[Pass condition]
First DUT Probe's target_proto_ip is inside 169.254.1.0..169.254.254.255.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_target_ip_in_reserved_range — Probe target is in the first or last 256 (169.254.0.* or 169.254.255.*)
• Fail_timeout — DUT did not emit any ARP Probe within the deadline

verdicts.Pass: DUT picked a Link-Local in the usable range — normal
verdicts.Fail_target_ip_in_reserved_range: Probe targets the reserved first/last 256 of 169.254/16
verdicts.Fail_timeout: DUT did not emit any ARP Probe within the deadline
